reason: Heating rocky planetesimals seems like a useful first step toward separating their stone and metal.
expectation: Radioactive heating may melt or alter the rocky bodies, though further steps will probably be needed to expose their interiors.

alternatives.reason: Heating icy bodies could advance the water-in-rock goal, but I'll follow the rocky branch first.

effect: The rocky planetesimal has melted, making gravitational separation of its materials plausible.
reaction: The distinction that not all asteroids melt is useful.
reason: Gravity may separate the melted body's metal and rock, advancing the goal of exposing its interior.
expectation: Denser metal may sink toward the center while rocky material remains above it; collisions may still be needed to expose them.

alternatives.reason: Heating the icy bodies could advance the water goal, but I want to continue the rocky branch first.

effect: Gravity separated metal from silicate, creating a differentiated small world whose interior could be exposed by collisions.
reaction: It's satisfying to see density-driven separation occur before Earth forms.
reason: A collision seems the most direct way to break the body and expose its stone and metal.
expectation: The collision may produce exposed fragments of the differentiated interior.

effect: Heating melted ice inside the body, providing liquid water that can react with silicate rock.
reaction: The possibility of liquid water beneath a frozen exterior is interesting.
reason: The only offered combination brings water and silicates together to advance the remaining goal.
expectation: Water may chemically alter the silicates and become incorporated into minerals.

effect: Water reacted with silicates to form hydrated rock, but the remaining goal is not yet marked complete.
reaction: It is useful to see that hydrogen can be incorporated into minerals rather than remain as ice.
reason: The only offered combination may advance the remaining water-in-rock goal.
expectation: Open space may cool the altered rock or otherwise preserve it, though I'm unsure what will happen.

effect: Cooling preserved water-bearing asteroid material and completed the remaining goal, showing how hydrogen can reach rocky worlds without exposed ice.
reaction: The connection between hydrated minerals and water delivery is interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reacting liquid water with silicates was most worthwhile: it showed how water-related hydrogen can become part of rock.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cooling the differentiated asteroid felt less engaging because the role of open space was not clear until afterward.

surprise.text: I was interested that a frozen-looking body can conceal liquid water and water–rock reactions.

arbitrary.text: Using open space on the altered rock felt somewhat arbitrary before the result explained that it cooled.

continue.text: Yes. The links between asteroid interiors, meteorites and water delivery make me curious how those materials contribute to a growing world.
